newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX index surges to new record levels.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX index surges to new record levels.

text.p: Germany's DAX index surged to another record high on Wednesday, buoyed by overnight Wall Street gains that underpin the market ahead of Thursday's German national reunification holiday.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 20.77 points at 2,676.50 after hitting another new record at 2,680.10, which surpassed the old level set on September 26 at 2,672.59.
"There's no wonder why the market keeps moving higher when you look at the dollar and Wall Street," one trader said.

But some traders said there was a risk of profit-taking in post-bourse IBIS computer dealings as traders squared positions ahead of the long weekend since many market participants were expected to be away on Friday.
"The holiday may make some people hesitant to establish new positions and then leave for the weekend," another trader said. "It may be time to hold or take some profits."
Among specific shares, the firmer dollar helped to support chemical sector shares, with BASF AG and Bayer AG both advancing faster than the broader market.
BASF ended up 95 pfennigs at 49.35 marks while Bayer gained 98 pfennigs to 56.98 marks.
Bank shares failed to keep pace with the broader market, with Deutsche Bank up 10 pfennigs at 71.92 marks and Commerzbank up five pfennigs at 34.85 marks.
Shares in Daimler-Benz AG, the industrial giant that has led the way in implementing controversial new sick-pay laws, were up seven pfennigs at 84.05 marks.

Daimler's works council on Tuesday said protests over the sick pay law, which cuts pay during sick days to 80 percent of wages from 100 percent, at its Mercedes unit had so far cost the carmaker around 200 million marks in lost production.
